title: European Stroke Organization guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis - Endorsed by the European Academy of Neurology

recommendations.text: The guideline suggests using magnetic resonance angiography or computed tomography angiography for confirming the diagnosis of cerebral venous thrombosis.
The guideline suggests not screening patients with cerebral venous thrombosis routinely for thrombophilia or for cancer.
The guideline recommends parenteral anticoagulation in acute cerebral venous thrombosis.
The guideline suggests preferentially using low-molecular-weight heparin in the acute phase, and suggests not using direct oral anticoagulants.
The guideline recommends decompressive surgery to prevent death due to brain herniation.
The guideline suggests not using steroids and not using acetazolamide to reduce death or dependency.
The guideline suggests using antiepileptics in patients with an early seizure and supratentorial lesions, to prevent further early seizures.

Because of very poor quality of evidence, no recommendations could be made concerning duration of anticoagulation after the acute phase, thrombolysis and/or thrombectomy, therapeutic lumbar puncture, or prevention of remote seizures with antiepileptic drugs.

The guideline suggests that in women who suffered a previous cerebral venous thrombosis, contraceptives containing oestrogens should be avoided. It also suggests that subsequent pregnancies are safe, but that use of prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin should be considered throughout pregnancy and the puerperium.
